author: Stannis
text_post: So, lately I’ve been watching Jordan Peterson videos and the parts about the oedipal conflict and devouring mother hit particularly close to home.  All throughout my life my mother projected her abandonment issues on me and effectively intuitively cultivated an insurmountable co-dependance. I was effectively the proxy for the men in her life that left her in one way or another (my grandfather killed himself when she was young, my father cheated on her multiple times and she left him when, I nearly died as a child). She is highly anxious and overbearing and has a constant need for external validation (tied my shoelaces until I was thirteen, started to panic to the point hysteria when a family member put me on their shoulders or played around with me). I mean I never learned to ride a bike because of her and was subject to constant ridicule due to my close relationship with her. She consistently buys me stuff I neither need nor want because she is dependant on the validation she gets from a simple ‘thank you’ in order to assuage her fractured sense of self. This isn’t solely limited to me. She incessantly finds older family members that have become dependant to take care of. It's easy to rationalise her effectively doing everything for me as maternal love but ultimately it's purely egotistical as she needed a positive reaction to validate herself and gave no forethought to the long term consequences of her actions. I hate her with everything I got, but I am dependant on her for resources as she subconsciously saw to it that I never develop the capacity to acquire my own. The best thing that could happen to me would be her dying, both in terms of personal growth and financial self-sufficiency.  What does that say about me when I let such a sick, weak, neurotic and pathetic woman have this destructive impact on my life? The only logical conclusion is that I’m even weaker than her. The worst part is that her pathological tendencies didn’t impact her life in any particularly negative way, but did irreparable damage to mine. Throughout my teens, with every girl there was a mutual interest with the pervasive thought was ‘What would my mother think if you fell for her’, as if me having a romantic life would be a betrayal of her. I was also highly religious growing up (although not because of her influence), which certainly contributed to my viewing sex as a morally condemnable transgression. And I remember being 12 or 13 or so and having sex ed. The consequent realisation that she and my stepfather were having sex regularly was genuinely traumatic to me and I was distraught and cried for days until she lied to me depicting it in a way as if they were just mildly physically affectionate without penetrative sex. I also used to have a room directly adjacent to theirs and would occasionally hear them moaning at night, which was always distressing in itself even if I couldn’t really place it.  And I think this is what corroded my relationships with women. My interactions with potential sexual partners are marked by a sense of inferiority, not necessarily towards them but towards other men who are ultimately competition. I have no functional autonomy and in my late 20s I’m still very infantile in a lot of respects. I’m acutely aware that I have nothing to offer when compared to other guys and I feel thoroughly inadequate when it comes tackling the exigences of adult life. Which leads to self-sabotage with any interested woman. It’s always better to be the rejecter rather than the rejectee, because after the initial elation and physical attraction there will be a guaranteed loss of interest considering how much of a maladroit, stunted manchild I am. This is a whole I can’t get out of. I could drop my studies and try to get a job (if I even manage to pass the selection procedures), which would then effectively be an elephant graveyard scenario as I would get comfortable and drop any attempt at self-actualisation but at least it would give me the possibility to cut her toxic influence out of my life. It’s necessary to find a compromise between autonomy and self-actualisation, but I don’t think I have the energy or strength of character to manage finding a middle ground.  I long for the day where I can leave her abandoned on her deathbed, with no one there to be with her in her final hours. I appreciate that all my posts are less generalised topics but more self-centred venting, but, especially with this topic, it would be interesting to see how many of you had relatable experiences and could offer an input on how to actually build a life for myself. At first glance a dysfunctional relationship with the mother seems to be the common denominator among a lot of incel and FA communities.

author: ieatboogers
text_post: "Mom is/was a bitch from hell" is common around here.  My mother was crazy and perpetrated some of the worst mental cruelties on both me and my father, and he would never stand up to her (though he was happy to use his fists on me if I protested, among other occasions.) I've posted a number of horror stories on here before. It is mostly her fault that I was largely unsocialized, grossly underfed and sick much of the time when I was little, but my father shares some of the blame for his complicity (as well as his own ill treatment of me). I'm glad I don't have to deal with her any more. I have only minimal contact with her now, a few letters a year; hers are of varying lucidity. I haven't seen her in about 18 1/2 years and I think it unlikely that I will again.  I'll offer some advice if I can. I'd start by thinking "I don't give a fuck what my mother thinks of me or my actions, I am old enough to make my own decisions." Say it out loud and mean it. If you think she might try to pull you back from this attitude by withholding money or other needed resources, a job is your ticket to independence. I'll go into some more details tomorrow; it's late here and I have to get to sleep. To help me be more specific, tell me (or, if you've already posted this, post the link to where you wrote it): how old are you now? What are your current living arrangements? How's the local economy/cost of living where you are? What are you studying? How long until you're done? Are you any good at it? Do you want to be studying this, and work it that field later? Did you pick it, or were you pushed toward it? What kind of work are you willing and able to do, not necessarily for the rest of your life, but over the short to medium term? How much contact do you want to have with your family, ideally? Do you have any siblings? How are they doing in life? Talk to you tomorrow.

text_post: It’s odd to see how such antipodal ways of treating your child can have equally disastrous consequences. Both being sheltered and pampered on one hand and being abused on the other lead to social maladaptation and all the negative reinforcement it entails. A great part of the issue is the ambivalence of my relationship with my mother. I am dependent on her on the one hand, on the other hand she did tremendous and possibly irreparable damage to me. But then again there was no actual deliberation behind it, it was instinctive on her part, which is more a signifier of her own pitifulness rather than any malice.
